thread:
Maya: Heads-up — we need to finalize span naming + attribute set for LLM requests before we ship exporter/retention changes. Focus: model identifiers, token counts, cache hits, routing policy. Any quick takes?

Chris: +1. We should avoid sending full prompts. Use a hashed prompt_id or prompt_set reference instead.

Devin: Agree. Proposed attr keys (draft): llm.model.name, llm.model.version, llm.model.variant; llm.tokens.prompt, llm.tokens.generated, llm.tokens.total; llm.cache.hit (bool), llm.cache.key_shard (string, no raw key). Keep values primitives.

Ashley: Slight preference to namespace infra-specific fields under "redwood.*": redwood.routing.policy, redwood.quota.bucket. But keep model + token fields under llm.* so other consumers can reuse.

Maya: Good call. Also retention convo: SRE wants 7d spans to cut cost, ops wants 30d spans, metrics 90d. Can we do sampled full spans for 30d and aggregated-only for 90d?

Chris: That seems reasonable. Implementation idea: OTLP exporter supports two streams — full_spans and agg_spans. Flag: telemetry.exporter.retain_full_spans = true/false; and telemetry.exporter.full_span_ttl_days = 30. If false, only export agg events.

Devin: Note on payload size: token counts on every request blow up payloads if we also include other attrs. Keep token attrs numeric ints, no arrays. Consider dropping token attrs for very short spans (<=8 tokens) to save space and add sampling_reason attr.

Ashley: Security reminder: do NOT include user identifiers or prompt text. Use llm.prompt_hash and llm.prompt_length but bucket lengths to avoid leaking exact lengths, e.g. "<512","512-2048",">2048".

Chris: Draft attribute block below (for RFC):

```
# span attributes (recommended)
llm.model.name: string (e.g., "gpt-4o-mini")
llm.model.version: string (semver or commit id)
llm.model.variant: string (quantization/format hint)
llm.request_id: string (uuid)
llm.prompt_hash: string (sha256 hex)
llm.prompt_length_bucket: string ("<512","512-2048",">2048")
llm.tokens.prompt: int
llm.tokens.generated: int
llm.tokens.total: int  # derived
llm.cache.hit: bool
llm.kvcache.hit_count: int
llm.kvcache.prefix_match: bool
redwood.routing.policy: enum("latency","cost","region","hybrid")
redwood.routing.fallback_model: string (name only)
redwood.routing.selection_score: float  # internal scoring value
redwood.quota.bucket: string
telemetry.sampling.reason: string ("high_token_count","manual","heuristic")
telemetry.exporter.name: string ("otlp","influx","internal")
telemetry.exporter.retain_full_spans: bool
telemetry.exporter.full_span_ttl_days: int
```

ot-bot: otlp-exporter: retention policy applied in staging — full spans 7d, aggregated spans 30d (config: telemetry.exporter.retain_full_spans=true, telemetry.exporter.full_span_ttl_days=7) :white_check_mark:

Maya: Hmm we need an ops decision then. Can we compromise: default 7d for full spans, but auto-promote spans tied to incidents/rollouts to 30d via tag telemetry.exporter.promote=true?

Devin: That works. Also add telemetry.sampling.decider and telemetry.sampling.rate as attributes in traces so downstream can re-evaluate retention on ingest.

Ashley: For KV cache, important: never export keys. Use hit_count and anonymized shard id only. Example: llm.kvcache.shard = "s1" not the key.

Chris: Also add routing metadata for fallback chains so we can debug: redwood.routing.chain = "modelA -> modelB (fallback)" but keep it short and capped to 128 chars.

Maya: I'll draft an RFC with the above and push to eng-infra/telemetry. Will include examples and exporter config snippets. Thanks all :heart:

Devin: Ack — will add tests that ensure no prompt text appears in exported spans (unit + e2e).

Ashley: +1, and I'll add a small script to sanitize existing exported spans before importing into long-term store.

Chris: Good teamwork. Next step: RFC + small staging rollout with OTLP exporter feature flag.

Maya: filing RFC now -> https://redwood.internal/rfcs/telemetry-llm-span-conventions (will update).
